title: Six letters from a two-letter start
hook: One instruction copies six letters from two. Where do they come from?

knows: compressing runs of a repeated letter (runs-that-grow)
doesNotKnow: that 'copy what came before' is how zip files work
that a back-reference copy can overlap itself

misconception: You can only copy text that has already been fully written.
objective: The learner can explain that a decoder copies one letter at a time, so a copy can read letters it wrote earlier in the same instruction, and two numbers (back 2, copy 6) can stand for a long run.

claims.text: Starting from 'ab', the instruction back 2, copy 6, applied one letter at a time, writes 'abababab'.
claims.source: Builder's node run (scratchpad algo10-verify.mjs): out += out[out.length - 2] six times gives abababab.

claims.text: Copy steps 1 and 2 read the original letters a and b; from step 3 on, each copy step reads a letter written by this same copy.
claims.source: Builder's node run: source indexes for steps 1..6 are 0,1,2,3,4,5; indexes 0-1 are the original 'ab', 2-5 were written by steps 1-4.

claims.text: A back-reference is two numbers (how far back, how many to copy) standing in for a repeat; an overlapping copy rebuilds a whole run from one instruction.
claims.source: Ziv and Lempel 1977, 'A universal algorithm for sequential data compression', IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 23(3); RFC 1951 section 3.2.3 (the overlap rule: a copy's length may exceed its distance, with the X,Y,X,Y,X example; section 3.2.5 gives the length 3-258 and distance 1-32768 codes). Section corrected 2026-10-14 by the builder per the pass-19 note (was 3.2.5); RFC not re-opened by the builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 20): Pass 20 source audit: opened RFC 1951 (zlib copy, raw.githubusercontent.com/madler/zlib/master/doc/rfc1951.txt). The overlap note and the <length = 5, distance = 2> -> X,Y,X,Y,X example are in 3.2.3 'Details of block format'; 3.2.5 gives length 3..258 and distance 1..32,768. Source correct. Ziv-Lempel 1977 IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 23(3) not re-opened.

claims.text: This is the idea inside gzip and PNG.
claims.source: DEFLATE (RFC 1951) combines LZ77 and Huffman coding; gzip (RFC 1952) and PNG (RFC 2083 / ISO 15948) both use DEFLATE.

recall.question: A decoder has written 'xyz'. The instruction says: go back 3 letters and copy 6, one letter at a time. What has it written in total?
recall.why: Each copied letter is read from 3 back, and from the 4th copied letter on that is a letter this copy wrote. 3 + 6 = 9 letters.
